title: Anthropic Shares Details on How Claude’s New Watermarking System Works
summary: Anthropic has provided further details on its implementation of watermarking for text generated by its AI chatbot, Claude. The watermarking system, required under the EU AI Act’s Transparency Code, embeds undetectable patterns in AI-generated text that can be identified using a detection key. The company uses Google DeepMind’s SynthID-Text approach and plans to release a detection API. Light editing may not fully remove the watermark, but a complete rewrite likely will. Watermarking has minimal impact on code generation due to constraints in valid syntax and structure. The system does not affect output quality and is part of a broader industry trend toward transparency in AI-generated content.
key_points: Anthropic is implementing watermarking for Claude’s AI-generated text to comply with the EU AI Act’s Transparency Code.
The watermarking system uses Google DeepMind’s SynthID-Text approach, embedding undetectable patterns in text that can be identified with a detection key.
Anthropic plans to release a watermark detection API for public use.
Watermarking does not affect the quality or readability of Claude’s output; watermarked and unwatermarked text are indistinguishable to readers.
Light editing of AI-generated text may not fully remove the watermark, but a complete rewrite likely will.
Watermarking has minimal impact on code generation, as the model prioritizes functional correctness over arbitrary word choices.
The system is distinct from AI detection tools that rely on stylistic patterns or ‘tells’ in writing.
Other major AI model developers are also adopting watermarking as part of industry-wide transparency efforts.
